gap.title: The Gap
gap.premise: Every person carries all seven gifts, ranked from most to least dominant. Put two people's rankings side by side and the differences can be measured. That measurement is the Gap — and it predicts, with uncomfortable accuracy, how much translation a relationship is going to require.
gap.method: For each of the seven gifts, take the difference between where it sits in your ranking and where it sits in theirs. Add the seven differences together. The result runs from 0 (identical profiles) to 24 (perfect inversion).

bands.name: Same Grain
bands.line: You understand each other without translating.
bands.body: Communication is nearly effortless and agreement comes fast. The risk is not friction; it is agreement. You share the same blind spot, the same trigger, and the same flare — so under pressure you will not check each other, you will amplify each other. This band needs an outsider more than any other.
bands.watch: Confirmation. When you agree instantly, ask who is missing from the conversation.

bands.name: Working Gap
bands.line: Enough overlap to feel natural, enough difference to cover each other.
bands.body: The most productive band on the scale, and the most frequently taken for granted. You have real complementarity and enough shared instinct to access it without effort. Because it works without maintenance in ordinary conditions, most pairs here never build the protocol they will need in hard ones.
bands.watch: Complacency. This band holds until the first genuine crisis, then discovers it has no agreed process.

bands.name: Wide Gap
bands.line: Misreading each other is the default, not the exception.
bands.body: Nearly every conflict here is a translation failure before it is a values failure. You are usually not disagreeing about what matters; you are disagreeing about what the other person just said. Handled deliberately, this is the range with the widest coverage — between you, very little is invisible.
bands.watch: Attribution. Before you conclude what they meant, ask. You will be wrong more often than your confidence suggests.

bands.name: Inverted
bands.line: What you lead with is what they can barely see.
bands.body: Your first gift is at or near the bottom of their ranking, and theirs is at the bottom of yours. The highest friction and the highest complementarity in the same relationship. These pairs either become the strongest partnerships in an organization or the ones that end badly — the variable is whether the differences were made explicit early.
bands.watch: Goodwill as a strategy. Inverted pairs do not run on affection. They run on protocol: who decides what, in what order, by when.

laws.title: A low Gap is not a good score
laws.body: Two Catalysts will agree on the diagnosis in ninety seconds and burn the room down together. Two Lovers will agree to a decision neither of them actually wanted. The Gap measures distance, not health. What predicts a good relationship is not similarity — it is whether the difference is known and named.

laws.title: Pressure widens the Gap
laws.body: In a normal week people operate across several gifts. Under pressure, everyone collapses back to their first gift and runs its flare. A Working Gap on a Tuesday becomes a Wide Gap in a crisis. Score your relationships for the hard week, not the easy one — the hard week is functionally a different relationship.

laws.title: The shape matters more than the number
laws.body: A Gap of 14 spread evenly across seven gifts is a very different relationship from a Gap of 14 concentrated in two. The figure that predicts conflict best is not the total — it is the inversion count: how many gifts sit in your top three and their bottom three. Each one is a place where something obvious to you is genuinely invisible to them.

laws.title: Distance is coverage
laws.body: Every gift you rank low is a category of reality you do not process well. Someone whose ranking inverts yours is not your opposite; they are your instrumentation. The cost of that coverage is that you will find them exhausting, and the cost of avoiding them is that you will keep missing the same things.

blindExchange.title: The Blind Exchange
blindExchange.premise: The sharpest friction in any pair sits where one person's first gift is the other's last. Not disagreement — invisibility. Here is what that specific mismatch feels like from both sides.

items.youSee: A system that is plainly broken and a room that will not say so.
items.theyGet: Nothing. The urgency does not register as information; it registers as instability.
items.theyFeel: Destabilized by someone who cannot leave things alone.

items.youSee: Undone work everywhere, and who is going to end up doing it.
items.theyGet: No signal at all. The undone thing is not on their map as a thing.
items.youFeel: Used, and quietly angry about a task they never knew existed.
items.theyFeel: Blamed for a failure they cannot locate.

items.youSee: Ground that has not been tested yet, and the cost of stepping on it anyway.
items.theyGet: Delay. They are three moves ahead and cannot see what is being checked.
items.youFeel: Rushed into a decision you will be blamed for.
items.theyFeel: Held up by someone who will not commit.

items.youSee: A room going cold and the relationships cooling with it.
items.theyGet: Noise. The emotional temperature is not a variable they track.
items.youFeel: Like you are the only one keeping this alive.

items.youSee: What this costs, where it came from, and who is carrying it.
items.theyGet: Resources as ambient and roughly infinite.

items.youSee: The sequence, the owner, and the date the whole thing fails without them.
items.theyGet: The plan as optional background context.

items.youSee: Exactly how everyone in the room is actually doing.
items.theyGet: A channel they do not receive. It is not that they dismiss it — they cannot detect it.
items.youFeel: Unseen, in a room you are reading perfectly.
items.theyFeel: Accused of a coldness they have no evidence of.

pairs.title: The Uprooting and the Groundwork
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens and announces the change. The Servant absorbs the extra work it creates without mentioning it. The Catalyst reads the silence as agreement and pushes further. The Servant begins to tally. The Catalyst names the Servant's process as the obstacle and indicts it. The Servant collapses — and the collapse is the first the Catalyst has heard about any of it.
pairs.aSees: Obstruction dressed up as diligence.
pairs.bSees: Someone destroying work that was functioning, who will not be there for the rebuild.
pairs.breaker: The Catalyst names the cost of the change out loud before announcing the change. The Servant states the cost as a number before absorbing it. Both moves are small; neither happens by accident.

pairs.title: Conviction and Corroboration
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens, needing validation now. The Erudite qualifies, because the case is not yet sound. The Catalyst reads the hedging as cowardice and indicts. The Erudite corrects — precisely, and with the receipts — then seals. Both are now certain, and neither is available.
pairs.aSees: Analysis paralysis protecting someone who does not want to be accountable.
pairs.bSees: Someone acting on a hunch and calling it revelation.
pairs.breaker: Agree a deadline for the answer before the argument starts. The Catalyst gets a date; the Erudite gets a runway. Most of this conflict is a scheduling problem wearing a moral costume.

pairs.title: The Wound and the Warmth
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens and the room's temperature drops. The Enthusiast performs harder to bring it back. The Catalyst reads the warmth as evasion and indicts. The Enthusiast spins. The Catalyst scorches. The Enthusiast vanishes, and tells the story later as an escape.
pairs.aSees: Someone who will sacrifice the truth to keep a room comfortable.
pairs.bSees: Someone who will sacrifice people to make a point.
pairs.breaker: The Catalyst delivers the hard thing and then stays for the repair. The Enthusiast hears the whole sentence before beginning to smooth it. Truth needs the warmth to be receivable; warmth needs the truth to be worth anything.

pairs.title: The Leap and the Ledger
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens: this has to happen, and it has to be resourced. The Host rations. The Catalyst indicts the caution as faithlessness. The Host funds it, but now with conditions attached. The Catalyst scorches. The Host closes the hand for good.
pairs.aSees: Someone protecting a balance sheet while the thing that matters dies.
pairs.bSees: Someone spending other people's resources on their own certainty.
pairs.breaker: The Catalyst brings a number and a failure case, not only a conviction. The Host names the actual condition instead of slow-walking the decision. Ambiguity is what turns this into a character fight.

pairs.title: The Pivot and the Plan
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens: new truth, change course. The Strategist tightens. The Catalyst indicts the plan as an idol. The Strategist overrides. The Catalyst scorches. The Strategist freezes them out and finishes alone.
pairs.aSees: Someone defending a plan that reality has already invalidated.
pairs.bSees: Someone who mistakes every new idea for a revelation and has never finished anything.
pairs.breaker: Separate 'is this true' from 'does this change the plan.' They are two different meetings. Run the first without deciding anything. Run the second with a decision rule agreed in advance, while everyone is calm.
pairs.note: The highest-heat pair on the list. Both are certain, both are aimed at the outcome, and each experiences the other as the primary threat to it.

pairs.title: The Blade and the Safety
pairs.loop: The Catalyst sharpens. The Lover soothes and absorbs the impact. The Catalyst mistakes the smoothing for agreement and escalates. The Lover pleads — sideways, and days later. The Catalyst reads the emotion as manipulation and indicts. The Lover shuts down.
pairs.aSees: Someone who cannot handle reality.
pairs.bSees: Someone for whom being right matters more than the person in front of them.
pairs.breaker: The Catalyst asks a question and waits through the entire silence for the answer. The Lover says the true thing in the moment rather than absorbing it.
pairs.note: This pair does the most damage fastest, because the Lover's distress is silent and the Catalyst reads silence as consent. The Lover's real response arrives days after the Catalyst has moved on.

pairs.title: The Doing and the Deliberating
pairs.loop: The Servant absorbs and starts the work. The Erudite qualifies, unwilling to endorse the approach yet. The Servant tallies — carrying this alone again. The Erudite corrects the work after it is finished. The Servant collapses.
pairs.aSees: Someone thinking about the problem while other people solve it.
pairs.bSees: Motion mistaken for progress, and work that will now have to be redone.
pairs.breaker: The Erudite gives a provisional green light with a named review point. The Servant asks for the review before doing the work rather than after.

pairs.title: The Load and the Lift
pairs.loop: The Servant absorbs. The Enthusiast performs — celebrates the team, generates the energy, picks nothing up. The Servant tallies. The Enthusiast turns the tally into a joke. The Servant collapses. The Enthusiast vanishes, hurt and genuinely bewildered.
pairs.aSees: Someone who takes credit for the atmosphere while other people produce the results.
pairs.bSees: Someone whose martyrdom makes the entire room heavy.
pairs.breaker: The Enthusiast takes one concrete, unglamorous task and finishes it visibly. The Servant converts the resentment into a request within forty-eight hours instead of banking it.

pairs.title: Two Kinds of Giving
pairs.loop: Both give. Both keep score. Under pressure each discounts the other's currency. The Servant absorbs labor; the Host rations resource. The Servant tallies — they wrote a check, I did the work. The Host leverages. Both withdraw, each privately certain they gave more.
pairs.aSees: Generosity that costs nothing personal.
pairs.bSees: Someone who does the visible task and calls it sacrifice while ignoring who paid for it.
pairs.breaker: Each names the other's contribution in the other's own currency, specifically and out loud. 'That check meant this.' 'Those hours meant that.' The entire conflict is two ledgers that were never reconciled.

pairs.title: The Hands and the Plan
pairs.loop: The Strategist tightens and assigns. The Servant absorbs. The Strategist reads capacity as availability and assigns more. The Servant tallies. The Strategist overrides the complaint as noise. The Servant collapses — with no warning that either of them would recognize as one.
pairs.aSees: Someone who spends people and calls it leadership.
pairs.bSees: Someone who never raised a hand and then broke.
pairs.breaker: The Strategist asks for the number rather than the willingness: what would have to come off for this to fit? The Servant answers with a real limit instead of a yes.
pairs.note: The most common burnout pair in any organization: a leader who assigns and a worker who has never once said no.

pairs.title: The Quiet Pair
pairs.loop: Both absorb. Both go silent. Neither asks. The Servant does more; the Lover insists nothing is wrong. Resentment accumulates on both sides with no visible surface. The Servant tallies through sighs; the Lover pleads through hints. Neither is answered, because neither asked. Both shut down.
pairs.aSees: Someone who is upset about something and will not say what.
pairs.bSees: Someone who is doing everything and will not say what they need.
pairs.breaker: One of them has to ask a direct question and then wait through the silence. Nothing here resolves by escalation, because neither of them escalates.
pairs.note: The least visible and most durable resentment on the list. This pair can run for a decade without a single raised voice and without a single honest sentence.

pairs.title: Depth and Delivery
pairs.loop: The Erudite qualifies. The Enthusiast simplifies it for the room. The Erudite corrects the simplification, publicly. The Enthusiast spins away from the correction. The Erudite seals. The Enthusiast vanishes.
pairs.aSees: Someone flattening the truth for applause.
pairs.bSees: Someone who would rather be precise than be understood.
pairs.breaker: Build the message together with clear domains: the Erudite owns accuracy, the Enthusiast owns receivability, and neither overrides the other's territory.
pairs.note: A genuine complement, wasted more often than any other pair on this list. Almost every idea that changed anything needed both of these people.

pairs.title: The Study and the Spend
pairs.loop: The Erudite qualifies. The Host reads it as an inability to commit and rations. The Erudite corrects the Host's reasoning. The Host attaches conditions. Both withdraw, each certain the other is the unserious one.
pairs.aSees: Decisions made on instinct and cash flow rather than evidence.
pairs.bSees: An inquiry with no end date that never produces anything to act on.
pairs.breaker: Put a decision date and a decision rule on the calendar. The Erudite gets the interval; the Host gets the guarantee that it terminates.

pairs.title: The Question and the Order
pairs.loop: The Strategist tightens — the call has to be made now. The Erudite qualifies. The Strategist overrides and decides without them. The Erudite corrects afterward, from the record. The Strategist freezes them out of the next decision. The Erudite seals.
pairs.aSees: An advisor who will not advise, and then critiques.
pairs.bSees: A leader who wanted agreement rather than counsel.
pairs.breaker: The Strategist asks for the best answer available by a stated time and commits to acting on it. The Erudite commits to producing one, clearly flagged as provisional. Both have to accept that a decision made on incomplete information is not a failure of process.

pairs.title: The Head and the Heart
pairs.loop: The Lover soothes and does not say what is wrong. The Erudite answers the words and misses the signal entirely. The Lover pleads. The Erudite analyzes the feeling instead of receiving it. The Lover shuts down. The Erudite seals, having concluded the exchange was irrational.
pairs.aSees: An emotional response with no argument inside it.
pairs.bSees: Someone who treated their pain as a proposition to be evaluated.
pairs.breaker: The Erudite says: tell me the feeling first, and I will not try to solve it yet. The Lover leads with the need instead of the story.
pairs.note: Their information is genuinely in different formats. Both formats are real, and neither converts without effort.

pairs.title: The Vision and the Cost
pairs.loop: The Enthusiast performs and sells the possibility. The Host rations. The Enthusiast spins past the objection. The Host funds it with strings attached. The Enthusiast vanishes the moment the strings pull.
pairs.aSees: Someone who kills momentum with a spreadsheet.
pairs.bSees: Someone selling enthusiasm as though it were a plan, with someone else's money.
pairs.breaker: The Enthusiast brings the cost alongside the vision, unprompted. The Host states the actual number and the actual condition instead of stalling.

pairs.title: The Room and the Result
pairs.loop: The Strategist tightens. The Enthusiast performs to restore morale. The Strategist reads it as noise and overrides. The Enthusiast spins. The Strategist freezes them out of the decision. The Enthusiast vanishes.
pairs.aSees: Energy substituting for execution.
pairs.bSees: A plan that will be executed flawlessly by people who have stopped caring.
pairs.breaker: The Strategist gives the Enthusiast ownership of a real deliverable rather than of the atmosphere. The Enthusiast reports the number before reporting the mood.

pairs.title: Two Ways of Loving People
pairs.loop: The Enthusiast performs and keeps it light. The Lover soothes and does not say the hard thing. The real issue is never raised. The Lover pleads sideways. The Enthusiast spins. The Lover shuts down. The Enthusiast vanishes, genuinely surprised that anything was wrong.
pairs.aSees: A mood that changed without warning.
pairs.bSees: Someone who was never actually present for the depth of it.
pairs.breaker: Schedule the hard conversation, because neither of them will start it spontaneously. This pair does not need more warmth. It needs a calendar.
pairs.note: Warm, easy, and quietly dangerous. Both are relational, both are conflict-averse, and both need to be wanted — which means nothing difficult ever gets said until it is too late to say it well.

pairs.title: Stewardship and Command
pairs.loop: The Strategist tightens — the plan requires the resource. The Host rations — the resource requires a return. The Strategist overrides the condition. The Host attaches a heavier one. The Strategist freezes. The Host withholds.
pairs.aSees: Someone treating the mission as a portfolio.
pairs.bSees: Someone treating their provision as an entitlement.
pairs.breaker: Agree in advance what the resource is for and what evidence closes the loop. This conflict is almost always the absence of a stated return condition, not a disagreement about the mission.

pairs.title: The Gift and the Gesture
pairs.loop: The Host rations. The Lover reads the withdrawal of provision as a withdrawal of love. The Lover soothes and asks for nothing. The Host reads the silence as not being needed. The Host withholds. The Lover shuts down.
pairs.aSees: Someone who never says what they need and then seems wounded.
pairs.bSees: Someone who gives things instead of presence.
pairs.breaker: The Host gives ten minutes of undivided attention instead of a thing. The Lover names one concrete need out loud.
pairs.note: These two are spending different currencies, both sincerely. Neither has ever been told the other's is legal tender.

pairs.title: The Mission and the Person
pairs.loop: The Strategist tightens. The Lover soothes, complies, and says nothing about the cost. The Strategist reads compliance as agreement and pushes further. The Lover pleads. The Strategist overrides it as emotional. The Lover shuts down. The Strategist freezes, concluding they cannot be relied on.
pairs.aSees: Someone who agreed and then quietly did not.
pairs.bSees: Someone for whom people are line items.
pairs.breaker: The Strategist asks what this will cost you, and treats the answer as data rather than as resistance. The Lover says no out loud, once, and discovers that the relationship survives it.

mirrors.title: When the Gift Meets Itself
mirrors.premise: Two people with the same first gift have a Gap near zero, and almost everyone reads that as compatibility. It is not. It is a doubled strength with a doubled blind spot and no one in the room who can see around it. Same-gift pairs do not fail from friction. They fail from agreement.

items.body: They reach the diagnosis in ninety seconds and escalate each other past every off-ramp. Nothing gets built. Something gets burned, and both of them will describe it afterward as necessary.
items.needs: A third gift in the room with actual veto power.

items.line: Two ledgers, neither one read aloud.
items.body: Both do more. Neither asks. The debt compounds silently for years while the relationship looks, from outside and from inside, entirely healthy.
items.needs: A standing question, asked on a schedule: what did this cost you this week?

items.body: The conversation is genuinely superb. The decision never comes. Each provides the other with a perfectly respectable reason for one more round of investigation.
items.needs: An external deadline, imposed by someone who is not in the room.

items.line: Two performances, one audience, no substance.
items.body: The room is fantastic. Nothing hard is ever said. Both leave energized and neither leaves known, and the friendship holds beautifully until the first thing that cannot be charmed.
items.needs: A scheduled, structured conflict, with the topic named in advance.

items.line: Two vaults, each waiting for the other to open first.
items.body: Generosity becomes a standoff conducted with immaculate manners. Both are keeping score of who offered last, and both are certain it was them.
items.needs: One of them gives first, without conditions, and says so out loud.

items.body: They either split the territory cleanly or they fight until one of them leaves. Ambiguity about who decides is fatal in this pair specifically — far more than in any other combination.
items.needs: An explicit decision-rights map, in writing, before it is needed.

items.line: Two people absorbing everything, both waiting to be asked.
items.body: The gentlest and least honest relationship on the list. Every hard thing gets swallowed to protect the other person, who is doing exactly the same thing, for exactly the same reason.
items.needs: A rule: the hard thing gets said within twenty-four hours. Badly, if necessary.
